scope: All public reference packages; internal/vendor implementation packages excluded. Language/runtime-specific packages remain open until an idiomatic mapping is reviewed.
completion_rule: A package is complete only after operation-level capability mapping, implemented public declarations, runtime/error tests and relevant benchmarks have been reviewed. Module presence alone is partial coverage.

packages.review: All ten recorded declarations, including duplicate value/ideal-integer constant records, and returned hash/clone/binary-state capabilities have functional mappings. SHA-224 and SHA-256 share a generated four-word SIMD schedule and exactly sixty-four ordered rounds per block, with exact private word loads and remaining-length machine counters. Independent fixtures cover 132 digest/checkpoint cases, every requested two-chunk split through 129 bytes and selected larger padding/block boundaries, 160 arbitrary restored-state updates including wrapped counts and noncanonical unused tails, and 912 identifier/size cases. Rust passes twelve target tests including three shared profile checks, an explicit O2/RC-debug temporary-owner stress case, and actual kernel compilation for WebAssembly, AArch64 and big-endian PowerPC. The self-built compiler passes ten selected target checks, excluding the two explicit Rust cases. Both execution modes validate ordinary 32 MiB heap/8 MiB stack bounds and a separate 256 MiB poisoned-free quarantine with zero leaks, including retained branches, mutable-buffer isolation, precise error precedence, source continuations and a 64 KiB one-byte stream. Foreign execution is not claimed. Three constant/generation tests and three inventory tool tests pass; fixture bytes and the generated private suffix reproduce exactly. The existing digest regression target passes four Rust checks. Forty-eight public pipeline/control rows match independent SDK checksums; paired executables record a modest 32-byte whole-buffer improvement while retaining unsuccessful intermediate measurements. Exact source patches reproduce all measured intermediates. Whole-buffer hashing avoids the intermediate state and tail buffer; state rendering retains the original specialization shape. Constants and all public/private declarations have canonical module-owned documentation. Portable SIMD/scalar compression remains slower than optional hardware SHA instructions; small-input and immutable buffer allocation costs differ from the reference implementation. Functional completion does not assert hardware or allocation parity. The full stdlib goal remains open.

packages.review: All seven reference declarations have functional mappings. Independent wire fixtures, 924 finite-capacity/finalization cases, every byte in each digit position after a valid group, all two-chunk splits, expanding overlapping shorthand, preserved invalid-byte snapshots and checked offsets pass with both compilers. On malformed input the reference implementation resets reported counts after writing complete groups; independent successful non-final decoding of its valid prefix recovers those boundaries for the stronger prefix-preserving Cinch API. SIMD handles complete groups and eight control bytes; unsigned inline LLVM interval checks avoid snapshots for disjoint buffers. ARM64 and big-endian PowerPC compile the kernels without claiming execution there. Independent public pipeline checksums and retained timing/allocation ablations are reviewed; complete means functional coverage, not equal object mutation, allocation complexity or throughput. Existing stream adapters can still copy buffered output on small reads.

packages.review: All four recorded declarations (including two records of Size) and returned hash/clone/binary-state capabilities have functional mappings. Independent fixtures cover 46 digest/checkpoint cases, all two-chunk splits through 257 bytes and selected long segment boundaries, 414 arbitrary restored-state updates, and 60 malformed size/identifier cases. Rust also passes all twelve existing stdlib regression tests, including ARM CRC/big-endian kernel compile checks. The portable SIMD core now has a standalone home; the compatibility Text.Checksum module still includes CRC embedded assembly unsupported by the self-built frontend, an existing CRC integration limitation not repaired here. Twenty-four public pipeline/control rows match independent SDK checksums; paired frozen executables establish the local reduction improvement without claiming allocation/throughput parity. Large test corpus setup uses an LLVM identity to keep generation at runtime after the Rust compiler overflowed its stack on fully constant setup; that compiler limitation is not claimed fixed.

packages.review: All eleven recorded declarations, including duplicate constant value/ideal-integer records, and returned hash/clone/binary-state capabilities have functional mappings. Immutable tables support every reflected U64 polynomial and expose every base entry without mutable aliases. Seven independent complete tables, 350 digest/checkpoint cases, 525 arbitrary restored-state updates and 791 malformed-state cases validate identifier/size/table error precedence. Requested two-chunk splits cover every position through 65 bytes and selected larger boundaries, including 16383/16384/16385 and 64 KiB. Rust passes twelve target tests including three shared profile checks and an explicit O2/RC-debug ephemeral-owner stress case; the self-built compiler passes eleven target checks with that Rust-only case excluded. A strengthened nonzero branching/isolation case is rerun through both compilers. Both modes validate ordinary 32 MiB heap/8 MiB stack bounds and a separate 256 MiB poisoned-free quarantine with zero leaks, including a 64 KiB one-byte stream. Twelve Rust compatibility tests pass, with actual CRC SIMD/SWAR kernels compiled for 32-bit WebAssembly, AArch64 with/without CRC capability and big-endian PowerPC; no foreign execution is claimed. The compiler prerequisite preserves private U128 SIMD pair results. Prepared-table traversal uses exact remaining-length machine counters and retains both backing owners, removing natural-number/ownership runtime paths from the O2 word loop. Thirty-two public pipeline/control rows match independent SDK checksums; retained source patches and paired frozen executables record counter-only and polynomial table-selection gains. Eight-slice construction, copied serialization buffers and owned stream chunks have different allocation costs; functional completion does not assert allocation or throughput parity. The compatibility Text.Checksum facade still includes CRC-32 embedded assembly unsupported by the self-built frontend; standalone CRC-64 is validated independently. Full stdlib coverage remains open.
